key_insight: SWE-Serve is a new benchmark that measures whether agents can make production-correct inference-serving changes across an entire serving stack, not just complete local code tasks.
engineering_relevance: It gives engineering teams a practical way to evaluate agents on real production inference work, including API, runtime, and model-support changes with hidden tests and performance gates.
method: 53 repository-grounded tasks derived from recent SGLang production changes
Six inference-engineering families spanning model, runtime, API, and serving-stack updates
Evaluation on CPU or a single H100 GPU with hidden functional, regression, E2E, and calibrated performance tests
evidence_signal: Across 11 models and 31 configurations, the best result reached 75% mean pass@1, while E2E serving tests rejected about one-third of patches that passed other checks on the 19 tasks with E2E coverage.
watch_item: Results may still understate real-world deployment difficulty because the benchmark is centered on one serving codebase and selected production-change patterns.
paper_title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving
